newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait, AGIP sign Milazzo refinery deal.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait, AGIP sign Milazzo refinery deal.

text.p: Kuwait Petroleum Corp has taken a 50 percent share in Agip Spa's 300,000 barrels per day Milazzo refinery and purchased 330 of its service stations in Italy.
"The agreement provides for a 50-50 joint venture which will own and manage the Milazzo refinery..." KPC said in a statement sent to Reuters.

The statement did not give a value for the deal but said "the implementation of such an agreement is subject to the approval of (Italy's) Antitrust Authority which started examining this deal a few months ago."

Under the deal KPC subsidiary Kuwait Petroleum Italy will acquire 330 fuel stations in Italy with an annual throughput of about 500 million litres (110 million Imperial gallons) -- 1.5 percent of the Italian retail market.

The deal allows KPC to "re-enter the Italian oil refinery industry and will expand its retail activity in Italy," the statement said. KPC shut its refinery in Naples in 1993 and has since been trying to re-enter the market in southern Europe.
The deal also provides for the upgrading of the refinery in Sicily to produce higher quality products.
The venture would raise output from Kuwait's European refineries to about 250,000 barrels per day ((bpd.
